concerns.text: The logistic regression model predicts the static‑detector outcome but does **not** include the two metrics that actually drive the static heuristic (ast_depth and cyclomatic_complexity). Omitting these mediating variables can introduce omitted‑variable bias, making it unclear whether the reported effects of dependency_depth, semantic_scope, and syntactic_complexity are direct or merely proxies for ast_depth/cyclomatic_complexity. This threatens construct validity of the claimed “intrinsic property → static success” relationship.

The 3×3 binning (tertiles of syntactic_complexity × dependency_depth) yields roughly 44 instances per bin (≈400 total). McNemar’s exact test requires a reasonable number of discordant pairs; many bins are likely to have <10 discordant cases, resulting in very low statistical power and unstable p‑values. The plan should ensure a minimum count per bin or aggregate bins to meet power requirements.

Synthetic edge‑case instances are generated deterministically to span the three intrinsic properties, but the plan does not discuss how the synthetic distribution matches the real‑world distribution of those properties. Relying heavily on synthetic data may limit external validity of the logistic‑regression threshold and McNemar results, especially if synthetic code differs systematically (e.g., in token count or style) from real TIDE instances.

The EPV (Events‑Per‑Variable) check is performed, but the plan does not provide a priori sample‑size justification (e.g., expected number of positive static detections). If the number of positives is low, even the fallback Firth regression may be under‑powered, compromising the reliability of the 0.5‑probability boundary estimate.

The sensitivity sweep varies probability cut‑offs, synthetic depth distribution, and binning schemes, but it does not explicitly assess the impact of the omitted static‑heuristic metrics (ast_depth, cyclomatic_complexity) on the stability of the identified threshold. Without this, it is unclear whether observed sensitivity is driven by genuine intrinsic property effects or by hidden confounders.
